java.a: Java is a high-level, object-oriented, platform-independent programming language created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (1995), now owned by Oracle. "Write once, run anywhere" — you write code once and it runs on any machine that has a JVM.

java.q: What are the main features of Java?
java.a: Simple – no pointers, automatic memory management. Object-Oriented – everything is built around classes and objects. Platform independent – bytecode runs on any JVM. Secure – no direct memory access, bytecode verifier, security manager. Robust – strong type checking, exception handling, garbage collection. Multithreaded – built-in support to run many tasks at once. Portable, High performance (JIT compiler), Distributed, Dynamic.

The Java compiler (javac) converts.java code into bytecode (.class file), not machine code. That bytecode is read by the JVM, and every OS (Windows, Linux, Mac) has its own JVM. So the same bytecode runs everywhere.
Simple picture: Bytecode is like an English letter; each JVM is a translator who reads it in its own local language.
No. Java has primitive types (int, char, boolean, etc.) which are not objects. Also static members can be used without objects. That's why it's called "not purely" object-oriented.

java.q: What is the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?
java.a:
JVM JRE JDK Full form Java Virtual Machine Java Runtime Environment Java Development Kit What it does Runs bytecode JVM + libraries to run programs JRE + tools (javac, debugger) to develop programs Who needs it — Users who only run apps Developers
Easy line: JDK = JRE + Development tools; JRE = JVM + Libraries.
JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler is part of the JVM. It finds code that runs again and again ("hot code") and converts it into native machine code while the program runs, so it becomes faster next time.
Bytecode is the intermediate code produced by javac and stored in.class files. It is not for any specific CPU; the JVM understands it.

java.q: Explain public static void main(String[] args).
java.a: public – JVM must be able to call it from outside the class. static – JVM calls it without creating an object. void – it returns nothing. main – the fixed name the JVM looks for. String[] args – command-line arguments.

java.q: Can we run a Java program without main()?
java.a: Since Java 7, no. Before Java 7 a static block could run, but now the JVM checks for main first. (Java 21+ has preview "unnamed classes and instance main methods" which make void main() possible, but in interviews say: main is required.)

java.q: Can we overload the main method?
java.a: Yes. You can write many main methods with different parameters, but the JVM always starts from main(String[] args).

java.q: What are data types in Java?
java.a:
Two types:
1. Primitive (8): byte (1 byte), short (2), int (4), long (8), float (4), double (8), char (2), boolean.
2. Non-primitive / Reference: String, Arrays, Classes, Interfaces.

java.q: What are default values of variables?
java.a: Instance/static variables get defaults: int →0, double →0.0, boolean →false, char →'\u0000', objects→null. Local variables get NO default — you must initialise them, or you get a compile error.

java.q: What is type casting? Widening vs Narrowing?
java.a: Converting one data type to another. Widening (automatic): small → big. int a = 10; long b = a; Narrowing (manual): big → small. double d = 9.7; int x = (int) d; // 9

java.q: What are wrapper classes? What is autoboxing/unboxing?
java.a: Wrapper classes convert primitives into objects: int→Integer, char→Character, double→Double, etc. Needed because collections store only objects. Autoboxing: primitive → object automatically. Integer x = 5; Unboxing: object → primitive automatically. int y = x;

java.q: What is the Integer cache? (Tricky) Integer a = 127, b = 127; System.out.println(a == b); // true Integer c = 128, d = 128; System.out.println(c == d); // false
java.a: Java caches Integer objects from -128 to 127. Inside that range the same object is reused, so == is true. Outside, new objects are created. Always compare wrappers with.equals().

java.q: What are variables types in Java?
java.a: Local – inside a method; lives only while the method runs. Instance – inside class, outside methods; each object has its own copy. Static (class) variable – one copy shared by all objects.
Arithmetic (+ - * / %), Relational (==!= > <), Logical (&& ||!), Bitwise (& | ^ ~ << >> >>>), Assignment (= += -=), Unary (++ --), Ternary (?:), instanceof.
i++ uses the value first, then increases. ++i increases first, then uses. int i = 5; int a = i++; // a=5, i=6 int j = 5; int b = ++j; // b=6, j=6
>> is signed right shift (keeps the sign bit). >>> is unsigned right shift (fills with 0). Matters for negative numbers.
if, if-else, switch (decision); for, while, do-while, enhanced for-each (loops); break, continue, return (jump).
while checks the condition first (may run 0 times). do-while runs the body first, then checks (runs at least once).

java.q: What is the difference between break and continue?
java.a: break exits the loop completely. continue skips the current iteration and goes to the next one.

Yes, since Java 7. It works with byte, short, char, int, their wrappers, enum, and String. Java 14+ also has switch expressions with -> and Java 21 has pattern matching for switch. String day = "MON"; int n = switch (day) { case "MON" -> 1; case "TUE" -> 2; default -> 0; };

java.q: What are keywords in Java? Is goto a keyword?
java.a: Reserved words like class, static, final, new, this. goto and const are reserved but not used.

java.q: What are identifiers and naming conventions?
java.a: Names of classes, variables, methods. Conventions: classes PascalCase (EmployeeService), methods/variables camelCase (getName), constants UPPER_CASE (MAX_SIZE), packages lowercase (com.company.app).

java.q: What is an array? How do you declare one?
java.a: An array stores a fixed number of values of the same type in continuous memory. Index starts from 0. int[] nums = new int[5]; int[] marks = {90, 80, 70}; int[][] grid = new int[3][3]; // 2D array
length is a field for arrays (arr.length). length() is a method for Strings (str.length()). Collections use size().
Thrown when you access an index less than 0 or ≥ array length.

java.q: What is a package? Why use it?
java.a: A package is a folder-like group of related classes (e.g., java.util). It avoids name conflicts, organises code, and controls access.
Modifier Same class Same package Subclass (other pkg) Everywhere private ✘ ✘ ✘ default (none) ✘ ✘ protected ✘ public

java.q: What is OOP? What are the 4 pillars?
java.a:
Object-Oriented Programming organises code around objects (real-world things with data + behaviour). The 4 pillars:
1. Encapsulation – wrap data and methods together; hide data using private + getters/setters.
2. Inheritance – child class reuses parent class properties (extends).
3. Polymorphism – one name, many forms (overloading, overriding).
4. Abstraction – show only what is needed, hide the details (abstract class, interface). Real example: A car — you use steering and brake (abstraction), the engine is sealed inside (encapsulation), a SportsCar is a Car (inheritance), and start() works differently in petrol and electric cars (polymorphism).

java.q: What is a class and an object?
java.a: A class is a blueprint (like a house plan). An object is a real thing made from that blueprint (the actual house). One class → many objects. class Student { String name; void study() { System.out.println(name + " studies"); } } Student s = new Student(); s.name = "Ravi"; s.study();

java.q: How many ways can we create an object in Java?
java.a: 1) new keyword, 2) Class.forName().getDeclaredConstructor().newInstance() (reflection), 3) clone(), 4) Deserialization, 5) Factory methods.

A special method that runs automatically when an object is created, used to initialise it. Same name as the class, no return type. Default constructor – added by compiler if you don't write any. No-arg constructor – written by you, no parameters. Parameterised constructor – takes values.
Constructor Method Same name as class Any name No return type Must have return type (or void) Called automatically with new Called explicitly Not inherited Inherited

java.q: What is constructor overloading and constructor chaining?
java.a: Overloading = many constructors with different parameters. Chaining = one constructor calls another using this() (same class) or super() (parent class). this() /super() must be the first line.

java.q: Can a constructor be private? Why?
java.a: Yes. Used in Singleton pattern and utility classes so nobody outside can create objects.
this refers to the current object. Used to separate instance variables from parameters (this.name = name), call another constructor (this()), or pass the current object.
super refers to the parent class. Used to call parent constructor super(), parent method super.show(), or parent variable super.x.

java.q: What is inheritance? What types does Java support?
java.a: A child class gets fields and methods of a parent class using extends → code reuse ("IS-A" relationship: Dog IS-A Animal). Types: Single, Multilevel, Hierarchical supported with classes. Multiple and Hybrid only through interfaces.

java.q: Why doesn't Java support multiple inheritance with classes?
java.a: Because of the Diamond Problem. If class C extends A and B, and both have show(), Java wouldn't know which one to use. To avoid confusion, Java allows multiple inheritance only with interfaces (and if two default methods clash, the class must override it).

One thing behaving in many forms.
1. Compile-time (static) – Method overloading. Decided by compiler.
2. Runtime (dynamic) – Method overriding. Decided by JVM at runtime based on the actual object.

Overloading Overriding Same method name, different parameters Same name, same parameters Same class Parent and child class Compile-time polymorphism Runtime polymorphism Return type can differ Return type same (or covariant subtype) static/private/final can be overloaded static/private/final cannot be overridden class Calc { int add(int a,int b){return a+b;} double add(double a,double b){return a+b;} } // overloading class Animal { void sound(){System.out.println("...");} } class Dog extends Animal { @Override void sound(){System.out.println("Bark");} } // overriding Animal a = new Dog(); a.sound(); // Bark (runtime decision)
No. If a child defines the same static method, it's called method hiding, not overriding. Static methods belong to the class, not the object.

java.q: Can we override private or final methods?
java.a: No. Private methods aren't visible to the child. Final methods are locked on purpose.
An overriding method can return a subtype of the parent method's return type. E.g., parent returns Animal, child returns Dog.

java.q: What is dynamic method dispatch / upcasting?
java.a: A parent reference holding a child object: Animal a = new Dog();. At runtime the JVM calls the Dog's version of the overridden method. This is how runtime polymorphism works.

Keeping data private and giving controlled access through public getters/setters. Like a medicine capsule — the medicine (data) is safe inside. class Account { private double balance; public double getBalance(){ return balance; } public void deposit(double amt){ if(amt>0) balance += amt; } } Benefits: data security, validation, easy to change internals later.

java.q: What is abstraction? How is it achieved?
java.a: Hiding implementation details and showing only the functionality. Example: you press an ATM button without knowing the bank's internal code. Achieved using abstract classes (0–100%) and interfaces (100% before Java 8).

A class declared with abstract. It cannot be instantiated, can have abstract methods (no body) and normal methods, constructors, and variables. A child must implement all abstract methods (or be abstract itself). abstract class Shape { abstract double area(); void info(){ System.out.println("Shape"); } } class Circle extends Shape { double r=2; double area(){ return 3.14*r*r; } }

A contract that says what a class must do, not how. All fields are public static final. Methods are abstract by default; since Java 8 it can have default and static methods; since Java 9 private methods. A class uses implements, and can implement many interfaces.

Abstract class Interface abstract keyword, extends interface keyword, implements Can have constructors No constructors Any type of variables Only public static final constants A class can extend only one A class can implement many Use when classes share common code/state Use to define a capability/contract (e.g., Comparable, Runnable)

java.q: What are default and static methods in interfaces (Java 8)?
java.a: Default methods have a body and let you add new methods to an interface without breaking existing classes. Static methods belong to the interface and are called with InterfaceName.method().
An empty interface (no methods) that gives a signal to JVM/compiler. Examples: Serializable, Cloneable, RandomAccess. Nowadays annotations are often used instead.
An interface with exactly one abstract method. It can be used with lambda expressions. Marked with @FunctionalInterface. Examples: Runnable, Comparator, Predicate, Function, Consumer, Supplier.

java.q: What is association, aggregation, and composition?
java.a: All are "HAS-A" relationships. Association – general relationship (Teacher ↔ Student). Aggregation – weak HAS-A; child can live without parent (Department has Teachers; teachers exist even if the dept closes). Composition – strong HAS-A; child dies with parent (House has Rooms; no house → no rooms).
IS-A = inheritance (Car extends Vehicle). HAS-A = one class has another as a field (Car has Engine). Prefer composition over inheritance for flexible design.

static means it belongs to the class, not to objects. One shared copy. static variable – shared by all objects (e.g., company name). static method – called without an object; cannot use this or non-static members directly. static block – runs once when the class loads. static nested class – inner class that doesn't need an outer object.

java.q: Why is the main method static?
java.a: So the JVM can call it without creating an object of the class.
final variable – value can't change (constant). final method – can't be overridden. final class – can't be extended (e.g., String).

java.q: Difference between final, finally, and finalize?
java.a: final – keyword for constant/no-override/no-inherit. finally – block that always runs after try/catch (used to close resources). finalize() – method called by GC before destroying an object (deprecated since Java 9, don't use).

java.q: What is an instance initializer block?
java.a: A { } block inside a class that runs every time an object is created, before the constructor body. Static block runs once at class loading.

java.q: Order of execution: static block, instance block, constructor?
java.a: Static block (once, at class load) → Instance block → Constructor. Parent's run before child's.
Checks if an object is of a certain type. Java 16+ supports pattern matching: if (obj instanceof String s) { System.out.println(s.length()); }

java.q: What is an inner class? Types?
java.a:
A class inside another class.
1. Member inner class – non-static, needs an outer object.
2. Static nested class – no outer object needed.
3. Local inner class – inside a method.
4. Anonymous inner class – no name, created on the spot (e.g., for an interface implementation).

java.q: What is the Object class? Its important methods?
java.a: Object is the parent of every class in Java. Important methods: equals(), hashCode(), toString(), getClass(), clone(), wait(), notify(), notifyAll(), finalize().

== compares references (same memory object?)..equals() compares content (same value?) if the class overrides it (String does). String a = new String("hi"), b = new String("hi"); a == b; // false (different objects) a.equals(b); // true (same content)

java.q: What is the equals() and hashCode() contract?
java.a:
1. If two objects are equal (equals() true), they must have the same hashCode().
2. Same hashCode does NOT mean equal (collision is allowed).
3. If you override equals(), you must override hashCode(). Otherwise HashMap/HashSet will behave wrongly (duplicates or can't find keys).
Returns a string representation of an object. Default prints ClassName@hashcode. We override it to print useful info.

java.q: What is shallow copy vs deep copy?
java.a: Shallow copy copies the object but shares inner objects (changes in inner objects affect both). Deep copy copies everything including inner objects (fully independent). clone() does shallow copy by default.
A special type for a fixed set of constants: enum Status { ACTIVE, INACTIVE, BLOCKED }. Enums can have fields, constructors, and methods, and are type-safe.
A short way to create immutable data classes. Java auto-generates constructor, getters, equals, hashCode, toString. record User(String name, int age) {} User u = new User("Anu", 22); u.name();
They restrict which classes can extend them: sealed class Shape permits Circle, Square {}. Gives control over the class hierarchy.
Local variable type inference. var list = new ArrayList<String>(); The compiler figures out the type. Only for local variables.

java.q: What is a String? Why is String immutable?
java.a:
A String is a sequence of characters and is an object in Java. It is immutable — once created, it can't be changed; any change creates a new String. Why immutable:
1. String Pool – many variables can safely share one object.
2. Security – used in passwords, URLs, DB connections; nobody can change it midway.
3. Thread-safe – no sync needed.
4. Hashcode caching – great as HashMap keys.

java.q: What is the String Constant Pool?
java.a: A special memory area inside the heap where string literals are stored. If the same literal already exists, Java reuses it instead of creating a new one. String s1 = "java"; String s2 = "java"; // same object from pool → s1==s2 true String s3 = new String("java"); // new object in heap → s1==s3 false

java.q: How many objects are created by String s = new String("hello");?
java.a: Up to 2 — one in the String Pool (if "hello" isn't already there) and one in the heap (because of new).
Returns the pooled version of a string. new String("a").intern() == "a" → true.

String StringBuilder StringBuffer Immutable Mutable Mutable Thread-safe (because immutable) Not thread-safe Thread-safe (synchronized) Slow for many changes Fastest Slower than Builder Use for fixed text Use in single thread loops Use when many threads modify

s = s + i in a loop creates a new String every time (wastes memory). StringBuilder changes the same object. StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) sb.append(i); System.out.println(sb); // 01234

length(), charAt(), substring(), indexOf(), contains(), equals(), equalsIgnoreCase(), compareTo(), toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), trim(), strip(), split(), replace(), isEmpty(), isBlank(), join(), chars(), repeat().
String s = "hello"; String r1 = new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString(); // Without built-in: String r2 = ""; for (int i = s.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) r2 += s.charAt(i);

java.q: Check if a String is palindrome.
java.a: boolean isPal(String s){ int i=0, j=s.length()-1; while(i<j){ if(s.charAt(i)!=s.charAt(j)) return false; i++; j--; } return true; }

Map<Character,Integer> map = new HashMap<>(); for (char c: "banana".toCharArray()) map.put(c, map.getOrDefault(c, 0) + 1); // Java 8: "banana".chars().mapToObj(c->(char)c) //.collect(Collectors.groupingBy(c->c, Collectors.counting()));

java.q: Check if two strings are anagrams.
java.a: char[] a = "listen".toCharArray(), b = "silent".toCharArray(); Arrays.sort(a); Arrays.sort(b); System.out.println(Arrays.equals(a, b)); // true

String s = "swiss"; Map<Character,Integer> m = new LinkedHashMap<>(); for(char c: s.toCharArray()) m.put(c, m.getOrDefault(c,0)+1); for(var e: m.entrySet()) if(e.getValue()==1){ System.out.println(e.getKey()); break; } // w
equals() returns true/false. compareTo() returns 0 (equal), negative (smaller), or positive (bigger) — used for sorting alphabetically.

java.q: Why is char[] preferred over String for passwords?
java.a: Strings stay in the pool until GC and can't be cleared. A char[] can be wiped (Arrays.fill(pwd,'0')) right after use, so it's safer.
Multi-line strings using """. Useful for JSON/SQL in code.
An unwanted event during program execution that breaks the normal flow (e.g., dividing by zero, file not found). Exception handling lets the program handle it gracefully instead of crashing.

Throwable is the root → two children: Error – serious problems we usually can't handle (OutOfMemoryError, StackOverflowError). Exception – problems we can handle. Checked (compile time): IOException, SQLException, FileNotFoundException, ClassNotFoundException. Unchecked (RuntimeException, runtime): NullPointerException, ArithmeticException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, NumberFormatException, ClassCastException.

Checked Unchecked Checked by compiler Not checked by compiler Must handle with try-catch or throws Handling optional Usually outside problems (file, network, DB) Usually programming mistakes (null, bad index)
Error = system-level, not recoverable (JVM out of memory). Exception = application-level, recoverable.

java.q: Explain try, catch, finally, throw, throws.
java.a: try – code that may fail. catch – handles the exception. finally – always runs (cleanup). throw – manually throw one exception: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Bad age"); throws – declares in the method signature that it may throw: void read() throws IOException.
throw throws Inside method body In method signature Throws one exception object Declares one or more exception classes Followed by an instance Followed by class names

java.q: Will finally run if there is a return in try?
java.a: Yes, finally still runs before the method returns. It does not run only if System.exit() is called or the JVM crashes.

java.q: Can we have try without catch?
java.a: Yes — try-finally or try-with-resources is allowed. But try alone is not allowed.

Java 7 feature that auto-closes resources (files, DB connections) that implement AutoCloseable. No need for finally. try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new FileReader("a.txt"))) { System.out.println(br.readLine()); } catch (IOException e) { e.printStackTrace(); }
Catch many exceptions in one block: catch (IOException | SQLException e).
Child exceptions first, parent last. catch(Exception e) before catch(IOException e) gives a compile error (unreachable).

java.q: How to create a custom exception?
java.a: class InsufficientBalanceException extends RuntimeException { public InsufficientBalanceException(String msg) { super(msg); } } if (amount > balance) throw new InsufficientBalanceException("Not enough balance"); Extend Exception for checked, RuntimeException for unchecked.
If a method doesn't handle an exception, it passes up the call stack to the caller, and so on, until someone catches it or the program ends.
A child's overriding method cannot throw broader checked exceptions than the parent method. It can throw the same, narrower, fewer, or any unchecked exceptions.

java.q: What is NullPointerException and how do you avoid it?
java.a: Occurs when you use a null reference (call a method on it). Avoid by null checks, Optional, Objects.requireNonNull(), "text".equals(var) style, and initialising values.
ClassNotFoundException (checked) – class not found when loading dynamically (Class.forName). NoClassDefFoundError (error) – class was present at compile time but missing at runtime.
Happens when the call stack is full, usually from infinite recursion (no base case).

A set of ready-made interfaces and classes to store and manipulate groups of objects. Main interfaces: Collection → List, Set, Queue; and Map (separate, not a child of Collection). Iterable └─ Collection ├─ List → ArrayList, LinkedList, Vector, Stack ├─ Set → HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet └─ Queue → PriorityQueue, ArrayDeque (Deque) Map → HashMap, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap, Hashtable, ConcurrentHashMap
Collection is an interface (root of List/Set/Queue). Collections is a utility class with static methods like sort(), reverse(), max(), unmodifiableList(), synchronizedList().
Array ArrayList Fixed size Grows automatically Stores primitives and objects Only objects length size() Faster, less features Many methods (add, remove, contains)

ArrayList LinkedList Dynamic array inside Doubly linked list inside Fast get by index O(1) Slow get O(n) Slow insert/delete in middle (shifting) Fast insert/delete (just change links) Less memory More memory (stores next/prev pointers) Best for reading Best for frequent add/remove
Default capacity is 10. When full, it creates a new array of 1.5× size and copies old elements into it.
Vector is synchronized (thread-safe, slower) and grows 2×. ArrayList is not synchronized (faster) and grows 1.5×. Vector is legacy.
List allows duplicates and keeps insertion order with index access. Set allows no duplicates, and order depends on the implementation.

HashSet LinkedHashSet TreeSet No order Insertion order Sorted order One null allowed One null allowed No null O(1) O(1) O(log n) Backed by HashMap Backed by LinkedHashMap Backed by TreeMap (Red-Black tree)
HashSet internally uses a HashMap. Your element is stored as a key (with a dummy value). Since map keys are unique (checked by hashCode() + equals()), duplicates are ignored.

java.q: How does HashMap work internally? (Most asked) Answer (in simple steps):
java.a:
1. HashMap stores data as key-value pairs in an array of buckets (default 16).
2. When you put(key, value), Java calculates key.hashCode(), then finds the bucket index: index = hash & (n-1).
3. If the bucket is empty → store the entry there.
4. If the bucket already has entries (collision) → it checks each entry with equals(). Same key → replace value. Different key → add to the list in that bucket.
5. Since Java 8, if a bucket has more than 8 entries (and table size ≥ 64), the linked list becomes a Red-Black Tree → search becomes O(log n) instead of O(n).
6. When entries exceed capacity × load factor (0.75) — i.e., 12 for 16 — the map resizes to double and rehashes.
7. get(key) → same hash → same bucket → equals() to find the exact key.
Simple picture: Think of a library with 16 shelves. The hash tells which shelf; on that shelf you check book titles (equals) to find your book.

java.q: What is a collision in HashMap?
java.a: When two different keys get the same bucket index. Handled by chaining (linked list → tree).
How full the map can be before it resizes. Default 0.75 (75%). A good balance between memory and speed.
HashMap: one null key, many null values. Hashtable: none. TreeMap: no null key (can't compare), null values allowed. ConcurrentHashMap: no null key or value.
HashMap Hashtable Not synchronized Synchronized Faster Slower 1 null key allowed No null key/value Java 1.2 Legacy (Java 1.0)
HashMap – no order. LinkedHashMap – insertion order (or access order, used for LRU cache). TreeMap – sorted by keys.

HashMap is not thread-safe. ConcurrentHashMap is thread-safe and fast: it doesn't lock the whole map — Java 8 uses CAS operations and locks only the individual bucket being written. Reads don't need locks. It's fail-safe (no ConcurrentModificationException).

java.q: Why should HashMap keys be immutable?
java.a: If a key changes after being stored, its hashCode changes, and you can never find it again. That's why String and Integer are great keys.

java.q: What is Iterator? Iterator vs ListIterator?
java.a: Iterator lets you loop and safely remove elements: hasNext(), next(), remove(). ListIterator (only for Lists) can move both directions and also add() /set().

Fail-fast (ArrayList, HashMap) throw ConcurrentModificationException if the collection is modified while iterating. Fail-safe (CopyOnWriteArrayList, ConcurrentHashMap) work on a copy/snapshot, so they don't throw.

java.q: How to remove elements while iterating?
java.a: Use iterator.remove() or list.removeIf(x -> x > 5). Don't call list.remove() inside a for-each loop.

Comparable Comparator java.lang java.util compareTo(o) compare(o1, o2) Natural (default) sorting, inside the class Custom sorting, outside the class Only one sort order Many sort orders class Emp implements Comparable<Emp> { int id; String name; public int compareTo(Emp e){ return this.id - e.id; } } // by id list.sort(Comparator.comparing(Emp::getName).thenComparing(Emp::getId)); // by name, then id

java.q: What is a Queue, Deque, PriorityQueue?
java.a: Queue – FIFO (first in, first out): offer(), poll(), peek(). Deque – add/remove from both ends (ArrayDeque, also used as a stack). PriorityQueue – elements come out by priority (min-heap by default), not insertion order.
Stack is legacy and synchronized. ArrayDeque is faster and recommended for stack (push, pop) and queue use.
Thread-safe list that creates a new copy on every write. Good when reads are many and writes are rare.

java.q: How to make a collection read-only / synchronized?
java.a: Collections.unmodifiableList(list), List.of(1,2,3) (Java 9, immutable), Collections.synchronizedList(list).
WeakHashMap – entries are removed by GC when the key has no other reference (used in caches). IdentityHashMap – compares keys using == instead of equals().

java.q: How to implement an LRU cache in Java?
java.a: class LRU<K,V> extends LinkedHashMap<K,V> { private final int cap; LRU(int cap){ super(cap, 0.75f, true); this.cap = cap; } // true = access order protected boolean removeEldestEntry(Map.Entry<K,V> e){ return size() > cap; } }

Operation ArrayList LinkedList HashMap/HashSet TreeMap/TreeSet get/search O(1) index / O(n) search O(n) O(1) avg O(log n) add at end O(1) amortized O(1) O(1) O(log n) remove middle O(n) O(1) after finding O(1) O(log n)

List<Integer> list = Arrays.asList(1,2,2,3,3,4); List<Integer> unique = new ArrayList<>(new LinkedHashSet<>(list)); // keeps order List<Integer> unique2 = list.stream().distinct().collect(Collectors.toList());

java.q: What are Generics? Why use them?
java.a: Generics let you write classes/methods that work with any type, with type safety at compile time. List<String> accepts only Strings — no casting, no ClassCastException. class Box<T> { T value; T get(){ return value; } } Box<Integer> b = new Box<>();
Generic type info is removed by the compiler after checking; at runtime List<String> and List<Integer> are both just List.

java.q: What are wildcards? extends and? super?
java.a: List<? extends Number> – can read Numbers (Integer, Double…), can't add. List<? super Integer> – can add Integers. Rule: PECS — Producer Extends, Consumer Super.

java.q: What is a thread? Process vs Thread?
java.a:
A thread is the smallest unit of work that runs inside a program. A process is a running program with its own memory. Threads live inside a process and share its memory — they're lighter and faster to create.
Example: Chrome is a process; each tab loading, downloading, playing video is like a thread.
start() creates a new thread and then calls run() in it. Calling run() directly just runs it like a normal method in the current thread — no multithreading.
NEW (created) → RUNNABLE (start called, ready/running) → BLOCKED (waiting for lock) / WAITING (wait/join) / TIMED_WAITING (sleep(ms)) → TERMINATED (finished).
Runnable Callable run() returns void call() returns a value Can't throw checked exceptions Can throw checked exceptions Used with Thread or Executor Used with ExecutorService → Future

A way to allow only one thread at a time to access shared code/data, to avoid wrong results (race conditions). Done with synchronized methods or blocks — the thread must get the object's lock (monitor). class Counter { private int c = 0; public synchronized void inc(){ c++; } }
When two threads change shared data at the same time and the result depends on timing. Example: two threads doing count++ can lose updates. Fix: synchronized, locks, or AtomicInteger.
A method locks the whole method. A block locks only the needed part — better performance: synchronized(this) {... }.
volatile ensures a variable is always read from main memory, not from a thread's cache, so all threads see the latest value (visibility). It does NOT make operations like count++ atomic.
wait() sleep() Object class method Thread class method Releases the lock Keeps the lock Must be in synchronized block Can be called anywhere Wakes by notify()/notifyAll() Wakes after time
notify() wakes one waiting thread; notifyAll() wakes all waiting threads on that object. Used for thread communication (producer–consumer).
t.join() makes the current thread wait until thread t finishes.

java.q: What is deadlock? How to avoid it?
java.a: Two or more threads wait for each other's locks forever. Thread 1 holds lock A and wants B; Thread 2 holds B and wants A. Avoid: always take locks in the same order, use tryLock() with timeout, keep synchronized blocks small, avoid nested locks.
Starvation – a thread never gets CPU/lock because others always take it. Livelock – threads keep reacting to each other and keep changing state but make no progress.

Instead of creating a new thread for every task (costly), a thread pool keeps a fixed set of reusable threads. ExecutorService manages them. ExecutorService ex = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(5); Future<Integer> f = ex.submit(() -> 10 + 20); System.out.println(f.get()); // 30 ex.shutdown(); Types: newFixedThreadPool, newCachedThreadPool, newSingleThreadExecutor, newScheduledThreadPool, and Java 21 newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor.
execute() takes Runnable, returns nothing. submit() takes Runnable/Callable and returns a Future.

Future holds a result that will be ready later; get() blocks. CompletableFuture (Java 8) is non-blocking and lets you chain tasks: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> getUser()).thenApply(u -> u.getName()).thenAccept(System.out::println);

java.q: What is ReentrantLock? How is it better than synchronized?
java.a: An explicit lock with more features: tryLock() (don't wait forever), timeouts, fairness, interruptible locking, multiple conditions. Must unlock() in finally.
Many threads can read together, but only one can write. Good when reads are much more than writes.
AtomicInteger, AtomicLong, etc. do thread-safe operations without locks using CAS (Compare-And-Swap). count.incrementAndGet().

CountDownLatch – one thread waits until N tasks finish (count reaches 0). Can't reset. CyclicBarrier – N threads wait for each other at a point, then all continue. Reusable. Semaphore – limits how many threads can access a resource at once (e.g., 3 DB connections).
Gives each thread its own copy of a variable. Used for user session/transaction info per request. Remember to remove() it in thread pools.
A background thread (like GC) that doesn't stop the JVM from exiting. t.setDaemon(true) before start().
Very lightweight threads managed by the JVM, not the OS. You can create millions of them. Perfect for I/O-heavy apps (web servers, DB calls). Thread.startVirtualThread(() ->...).
A producer adds items to a shared buffer, a consumer takes them. The producer must wait when full, the consumer when empty. Easiest solution: BlockingQueue (put() / take() wait automatically).
A pool that splits a big task into small sub-tasks (fork), runs them in parallel, and combines results (join). Uses work-stealing. Parallel streams use it.

java.q: Print odd and even numbers using two threads (coding).
java.a: class Printer { int n = 1; final int max = 10; synchronized void print(boolean odd) throws InterruptedException { while (n <= max) { while ((n % 2 == 1)!= odd) wait(); if (n <= max) System.out.println(Thread.currentThread().getName() + ": " + n++); notifyAll(); } } } Printer p = new Printer(); new Thread(() -> { try { p.print(true); } catch (Exception e) {} }, "Odd").start(); new Thread(() -> { try { p.print(false); } catch (Exception e) {} }, "Even").start();

java.q: What are the main features of Java 8?
java.a: Lambda expressions, Functional interfaces, Stream API, Method references, Default & static methods in interfaces, Optional, New Date-Time API (java.time), CompletableFuture, forEach(), Nashorn JS engine (removed later).

A short, anonymous function — a way to pass behaviour as data. Syntax: (parameters) -> expression. // Old way Runnable r = new Runnable(){ public void run(){ System.out.println("Hi"); } }; // Lambda Runnable r2 = () -> System.out.println("Hi"); Comparator<String> c = (a, b) -> a.length() - b.length();

java.q: What are the built-in functional interfaces?
java.a: Interface Method Use Predicate<T> test(T) → boolean Conditions/filtering Function<T,R> apply(T) → R Transform Consumer<T> accept(T) → void Do something (print) Supplier<T> get() → T Provide a value BiFunction<T,U,R> apply(T,U) Two inputs UnaryOperator<T> / BinaryOperator<T> same type in/out Math ops
A shorter lambda that points to an existing method using::. Types: static (Integer::parseInt), instance (System.out::println), arbitrary object (String::toUpperCase), constructor (ArrayList::new).

A way to process collections in a functional, declarative style (what to do, not how). A stream doesn't store data and doesn't change the source. Intermediate ops (lazy, return stream): filter, map, flatMap, sorted, distinct, limit, skip, peek. Terminal ops (start processing): collect, forEach, count, reduce, min, max, anyMatch, allMatch, findFirst. List<Integer> nums = List.of(1,2,3,4,5,6); List<Integer> evenSquares = nums.stream().filter(n -> n % 2 == 0).map(n -> n * n).toList(); // [4,16,36]
Collection stores data (eager); Stream processes data (lazy), can be used only once, and supports parallel processing easily.

map() transforms each element 1-to-1. flatMap() transforms each element into a stream and flattens everything into one stream. List<List<Integer>> l = List.of(List.of(1,2), List.of(3,4)); l.stream().flatMap(List::stream).toList(); // [1,2,3,4]

java.q: What are lazy evaluation and short-circuit operations?
java.a: Intermediate operations don't run until a terminal operation is called. Short- circuit ops (findFirst, anyMatch, limit) stop early once the answer is found.
findFirst() always returns the first element. findAny() may return any — faster in parallel streams.
Combines all elements into one result. nums.stream().reduce(0, Integer::sum) → sum.
Parallel stream splits work across multiple CPU cores (ForkJoinPool). Good for big CPU-heavy data; bad for small data, order-dependent tasks, or shared mutable state.

A container that may or may not hold a value — helps avoid NullPointerException. Methods: of(), ofNullable(), empty(), isPresent(), ifPresent(), orElse(), orElseGet(), orElseThrow(), map(). Optional<User> u = repo.findById(1); String name = u.map(User::getName).orElse("Unknown");
orElse(x) always evaluates x even if a value exists. orElseGet(() -> x) only runs when empty — better if creating the default is costly.

java.q: What is the new Date-Time API?
java.a: java.time package — LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, ZonedDateTime, Period, Duration, DateTimeFormatter. Immutable and thread-safe (the old Date /SimpleDateFormat were not).

java.q: Features after Java 8 (9–21) you should know?
java.a: Version Feature 9 Modules (JPMS), List.of(), JShell, private interface methods 10 var 11 (LTS) String.isBlank(), strip(), lines(), repeat(), HTTP Client, run java File.java directly 14 Switch expressions, helpful NullPointerException messages 15 Text blocks 16 Records, pattern matching for instanceof 17 (LTS) Sealed classes 21 (LTS) Virtual threads, pattern matching for switch, record patterns, sequenced collections

1. Class Loader – loads.class files (Loading → Linking → Initialization).
2. Runtime Data Areas (memory): Method Area/Metaspace, Heap, Stack, PC Register, Native Method Stack.
3. Execution Engine – Interpreter + JIT compiler + Garbage Collector.
4. JNI – talks to native (C/C++) libraries.

Stack Heap Stores method calls, local variables, references Stores objects and instance variables Each thread has its own Shared by all threads Fast, auto-cleared when method ends Cleaned by Garbage Collector StackOverflowError OutOfMemoryError Student s = new Student(); → s (reference) is on the stack, the Student object is on the heap.
Bootstrap (core Java classes like java.lang), Platform/Extension, Application/System (your classes on classpath). They follow the delegation model — ask parent first.
The JVM automatically frees memory by removing objects that are no longer referenced. You don't need to delete objects manually. System.gc() only requests GC; it's not guaranteed.

java.q: How does GC work? What are generations?
java.a: Heap is divided into: Young Generation (Eden + Survivor S0/S1) – new objects. Minor GC runs often here. Old Generation – objects that survived many GCs. Major/Full GC here. Metaspace (Java 8+, replaced PermGen) – class metadata, stored in native memory. Most objects die young, so this split makes GC faster. Algorithm idea: Mark (find live objects) → Sweep (remove dead) → Compact (remove gaps).
Serial, Parallel, G1 (default since Java 9 – splits heap into regions), ZGC and Shenandoah (very low pause times, for large heaps).

java.q: When is an object eligible for GC?
java.a: When nothing references it: set reference to null, reassign reference, object created inside a method that ended, or islands of isolation (objects referring only to each other).

java.q: What is a memory leak in Java? How to find it?
java.a: Objects that are no longer needed but still referenced, so GC can't remove them (e.g., growing static lists, unclosed resources, listeners never removed, ThreadLocal not cleared). Find with heap dumps, VisualVM, JProfiler, Eclipse MAT.
Strong – normal; never collected while referenced. Soft – collected only when memory is low (caches). Weak – collected at next GC. Phantom – used for cleanup tracking after the object is finalized.
-Xms (initial heap), -Xmx (max heap), -Xss (thread stack size), -XX:+UseG1GC, - XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError.
Serialization converts an object into a byte stream (to save to a file or send over a network). Deserialization converts bytes back into an object. The class must implement Serializable.
A transient field is not serialized (e.g., password). After deserialization it gets the default value.
A version number for a serializable class. If it doesn't match during deserialization, you get InvalidClassException. Always declare it.
Serializable is automatic (marker interface). Externalizable gives full control with writeExternal() / readExternal() and needs a public no-arg constructor.
The ability to inspect and change classes, methods, and fields at runtime (even private ones). Used by frameworks like Spring, Hibernate, JUnit. Downsides: slower, breaks encapsulation.
Metadata added to code with @. Built-in: @Override, @Deprecated, @SuppressWarnings, @FunctionalInterface. Frameworks use custom ones like @Autowired, @Entity. Retention: SOURCE, CLASS, RUNTIME.

java.q: What is an immutable class? How to create one?
java.a:
An object whose state can't change after creation (like String).
1. Make the class final.
2. Make all fields private final.
3. No setters.
4. Initialise all fields in the constructor.
5. For mutable fields (List, Date), return copies in getters and store copies in the constructor. public final class Employee { private final String name; private final List<String> skills; public Employee(String name, List<String> skills){ this.name = name; this.skills = List.copyOf(skills); } public String getName(){ return name; } public List<String> getSkills(){ return skills; } }
System is a class, out is a static PrintStream object in it, and println() is a method of PrintStream.

java.q: What is JDBC? Steps to connect to a DB?
java.a:
Java Database Connectivity – API to connect Java with databases.
1. Load driver (automatic since JDBC 4).
2. Get connection: DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass).
3. Create PreparedStatement.
4. Execute query → ResultSet.
5. Close resources (try-with-resources).
PreparedStatement is pre-compiled (faster for repeated queries) and uses? placeholders, which prevents SQL injection. Always prefer it.

1. S – Single Responsibility: a class should do one job only.
2. O – Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification (add new classes rather than editing old ones).
3. L – Liskov Substitution: a child class should work wherever the parent works.
4. I – Interface Segregation: many small interfaces are better than one fat interface.
5. D – Dependency Inversion: depend on abstractions (interfaces), not concrete classes. (Spring DI follows this.)

java.q: What is the Singleton pattern? Write a thread-safe one.
java.a: Only one object of a class exists in the whole application (e.g., config, logger, DB pool). public class Singleton { private static volatile Singleton instance; private Singleton() {} public static Singleton getInstance() { if (instance == null) { synchronized (Singleton.class) { if (instance == null) instance = new Singleton(); // double-checked locking } } return instance; } } Easiest safe way: enum Singleton { INSTANCE; } (safe from reflection and serialization too).
Reflection (calling private constructor), serialization (creates new object — fix with readResolve()), cloning (override clone() to throw). Enum singleton avoids all.
A method creates objects for you based on input, so the caller doesn't use new directly. ShapeFactory.get("circle") returns a Circle.
Builds complex objects step by step, readable when there are many optional fields. User.builder().name("A").age(22).build(); (Lombok @Builder).

Observer – one object notifies many listeners (event systems, YouTube subscribers). Strategy – choose an algorithm at runtime (different payment methods). Decorator – add behaviour without changing the class (Java I/O streams). Adapter – make incompatible interfaces work together. Proxy – a stand-in object that controls access (Spring AOP, lazy loading). Template Method – parent defines steps, child fills some steps.

java.q: Swap two numbers without a third variable.
java.a: a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b;
int a = 0, b = 1; for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { System.out.print(a + " "); int c = a + b; a = b; b = c; }
boolean isPrime(int n){ if(n<2) return false; for(int i=2; i*i<=n; i++) if(n%i==0) return false; return true; }
long fact(int n){ return n <= 1? 1: n * fact(n - 1); }

java.q: Find the second largest number in an array.
java.a: int first = Integer.MIN_VALUE, second = Integer.MIN_VALUE; for (int n: arr) { if (n > first) { second = first; first = n; } else if (n > second && n!= first) second = n; }
int expected = n * (n + 1) / 2; int actual = 0; for (int x: arr) actual += x; int missing = expected - actual;

java.q: Reverse an array / move zeros to end.
java.a: // move zeros int j = 0; for (int i = 0; i < a.length; i++) if (a[i]!= 0) { int t = a[i]; a[i] = a[j]; a[j++] = t; }

java.q: Two Sum (find pair with target sum).
java.a: Map<Integer,Integer> m = new HashMap<>(); for (int i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { int need = target - nums[i]; if (m.containsKey(need)) return new int[]{m.get(need), i}; m.put(nums[i], i); }
int n = 153, t = n, sum = 0, d = String.valueOf(n).length(); while (t > 0) { sum += Math.pow(t % 10, d); t /= 10; } System.out.println(sum == n);
int lo = 0, hi = a.length - 1; while (lo <= hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (a[mid] == key) return mid; else if (a[mid] < key) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1; } return -1;
for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) for (int j = 0; j < n - i - 1; j++) if (a[j] > a[j+1]) { int t = a[j]; a[j] = a[j+1]; a[j+1] = t; }
String[] w = "I love Java".split(" "); Collections.reverse(Arrays.asList(w)); System.out.println(String.join(" ", w)); // Java love I
long vowels = "interview".chars().filter(c -> "aeiou".indexOf(c) >= 0).count();

Deque<Character> st = new ArrayDeque<>(); for (char c: s.toCharArray()) { if ("({[".indexOf(c) >= 0) st.push(c); else { if (st.isEmpty()) return false; char o = st.pop(); if ((c==')'&&o!='(')||(c=='}'&&o!='{')||(c==']'&&o!='[')) return false; } } return st.isEmpty();
Node prev = null, cur = head; while (cur!= null) { Node next = cur.next; cur.next = prev; prev = cur; cur = next; } head = prev;

java.q: Detect a loop in a linked list.
java.a: Floyd's algorithm — slow pointer moves 1 step, fast moves 2. If they meet, there's a loop.

python.a: Python is a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose language created by Guido van Rossum (1991). It is famous for simple, readable syntax. Used in web development (Django, Flask, FastAPI), data science, AI/ML, automation, scripting, and cloud (AWS Lambda).
Easy to read, interpreted, dynamically typed, object-oriented + functional, huge standard library, cross-platform, open source, large community, supports many third-party packages (pip).
Both, in a way. Python code is first compiled to bytecode (.pyc files) and then the Python Virtual Machine (PVM) interprets that bytecode line by line. So we usually call it an interpreted language.
You don't declare variable types. The type is decided at runtime and can change: x = 5 then x = "hi" is fine. Python is also strongly typed — "5" + 5 gives an error (no automatic mixing).
Python's official style guide — 4-space indentation, snake_case for functions/variables, PascalCase for classes, max ~79 characters per line, spaces around operators.

python.q: Why is indentation important in Python?
python.a: Python uses indentation (spaces) instead of { } to define code blocks. Wrong indentation = IndentationError.

python.q: What are Python's built-in data types?
python.a: Category Types Numeric int, float, complex Text str Sequence list, tuple, range Mapping dict Set set, frozenset Boolean bool Binary bytes, bytearray None NoneType

Mutable (can change after creation): list, dict, set, bytearray. Immutable (can't change): int, float, str, tuple, frozenset, bool. a = [1, 2]; a.append(3) # list changes → mutable s = "hi"; s[0] = "H" # TypeError → str is immutable

List Tuple Mutable Immutable [1, 2, 3] (1, 2, 3) Slower, more memory Faster, less memory Can't be a dict key Can be a dict key (if items are immutable) Use for changing data Use for fixed data (coordinates, DB rows)

A collection of key-value pairs. Keys must be unique and immutable. Since Python 3.7 it keeps insertion order. Lookup is O(1) (uses hashing). student = {"name": "Anu", "age": 22} student["city"] = "Vijayawada" print(student.get("marks", 0)) # 0 (default if key missing)
An unordered collection of unique items. Great for removing duplicates and math operations: union |, intersection &, difference -. print(set([1, 2, 2, 3])) # {1, 2, 3}
Python's "no value" object (like null). Check with if x is None:.
== checks if values are equal. is checks if both variables point to the same object in memory. a = [1, 2]; b = [1, 2] a == b # True a is b # False
Arithmetic (+ - * / // % **), comparison, logical (and or not), identity (is, is not), membership (in, not in), bitwise, assignment (+=, walrus:=).
/ is normal division → float (7/2 = 3.5). // is floor division → rounds down (7//2 = 3).
Getting part of a sequence: seq[start:stop:step] (stop not included). s = "python" s[0:3] # 'pyt' s[-1] # 'n' s[::-1] # 'nohtyp' (reverse)
-1 is the last item, -2 second last, etc.
upper(), lower(), strip(), split(), join(), replace(), find(), startswith(), endswith(), isdigit(), isalpha(), count(), title(), format(), and f-strings: f"Hi {name}".

python.q: How do you take input and convert types?
python.a: age = int(input("Enter age: ")) # input() always returns a str

python.q: What are loops in Python? Does Python have do-while?
python.a: for (over any iterable) and while. No do-while — use while True: with break. Loops can have an else block that runs if the loop didn't break.
break – exit the loop. continue – skip to the next iteration. pass – do nothing (placeholder for empty blocks).
Generates a sequence of numbers lazily: range(start, stop, step). range(5) → 0 to 4.
for i, name in enumerate(["a", "b"]): print(i, name) # index + value for n, m in zip([1, 2], ["x", "y"]): print(n, m) # pairs items together
int(), float(), str(), list(), tuple(), set(), dict(), bool(). Implicit conversion also happens: 3 + 2.5 = 5.5.

python.q: What are truthy and falsy values?
python.a: Falsy: False, None, 0, 0.0, "", [], {}, (), set(). Everything else is truthy.

python.q: How do you define a function?
python.a: def greet(name, msg="Hello"): # msg has a default value return f"{msg}, {name}" greet("Monika")
Positional, keyword (greet(name="A")), default, variable-length *args (tuple), **kwargs (dict). Also positional-only (/) and keyword-only (*) markers.
*args accepts any number of positional arguments as a tuple. **kwargs accepts any number of keyword arguments as a dict. def f(*args, **kwargs): print(args, kwargs) f(1, 2, a=3) # (1, 2) {'a': 3}
A small, anonymous one-line function: square = lambda x: x * x. Often used with map, filter, sorted. sorted(people, key=lambda p: p["age"])
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4] list(map(lambda x: x * 2, nums)) # [2, 4, 6, 8] list(filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, nums)) # [2, 4] from functools import reduce reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, nums) # 10

python.q: How are arguments passed — by value or by reference?
python.a: Neither exactly — Python uses pass by object reference ("pass by assignment"). The function gets a reference to the same object. If the object is mutable (list), changes inside the function are visible outside. If immutable (int, str), reassigning inside doesn't affect outside.

python.q: What is the mutable default argument trap? (tricky) def add(x, lst=[]):
python.a: lst.append(x); return lst add(1) # [1] add(2) # [1, 2] ← same list reused! Default values are created once when the function is defined. Fix: use lst=None and inside if lst is None: lst = [].

python.q: What is scope? What is LEGB rule?
python.a: Python searches names in this order: Local → Enclosing (outer function) → Global → Built-in.
global x lets you modify a global variable inside a function. nonlocal x lets an inner function modify a variable from the enclosing (outer) function.
A function calling itself. Needs a base case. Python's default recursion limit is ~1000 (sys.setrecursionlimit).
Triple-quoted text at the start of a function/class/module that documents it. Access with func.__doc__ or help(func).
Optional annotations showing expected types: def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:. Python doesn't enforce them at runtime, but tools like mypy and IDEs use them. FastAPI and Pydantic rely on them.

A short way to create lists in one line. squares = [x * x for x in range(5)] # [0, 1, 4, 9, 16] evens = [x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0] Also dict comprehension {k: v for...} and set comprehension {x for...}.

python.q: What is an iterator? Iterable vs Iterator?
python.a: An iterable is anything you can loop over (list, str, dict) — it has __iter__(). An iterator is the object that gives the next value with __next__() and remembers its position; raises StopIteration at the end. it = iter([1, 2]); next(it) # 1

A function that uses yield to give values one at a time, pausing between them. It doesn't store all values in memory — great for large data or infinite sequences. def count_up(n): for i in range(n): yield i for x in count_up(3): print(x) Generator expression: (x * x for x in range(10**9)) – uses almost no memory.
return ends the function and sends one value. yield pauses the function, sends a value, and resumes from the same place next time.
[ ] builds the whole list in memory immediately. () creates a generator that produces values lazily — memory efficient.

python.q: How do you create a class and object?
python.a: class Student: school = "KL University" # class variable (shared) def __init__(self, name, marks): # constructor self.name = name # instance variables self.marks = marks def show(self): print(self.name, self.marks) s = Student("Ravi", 90); s.show()
self refers to the current object. It must be the first parameter of instance methods (Python passes it automatically).
The initializer (constructor) method — runs automatically when an object is created to set its data. (__new__ actually creates the object; __init__ initialises it.)
Class variable – shared by all objects (defined in class body). Instance variable – unique per object (defined with self.).

python.q: Instance method vs class method vs static method?
python.a: Instance method @classmethod @staticmethod First arg self First arg cls No special first arg Works with object data Works with class data; used as factory methods Utility function inside class

Yes — single, multiple, multilevel, hierarchical, hybrid. Python supports multiple inheritance with classes (unlike Java). class Animal: def speak(self): return "..." class Dog(Animal): def speak(self): return "Bark" # overriding

The order Python searches parent classes for a method in multiple inheritance. It uses the C3 linearization algorithm. Check with ClassName.__mro__ or ClassName.mro(). This is how Python solves the diamond problem.
Calls a method from the parent class (following MRO): super().__init__(name).
Not directly — the last defined method with the same name wins. We use default arguments or *args, or functools.singledispatch. Overriding is supported.

python.q: How is encapsulation done in Python?
python.a: By convention: _var = protected (internal use), __var = private (name mangling changes it to _ClassName__var). Python has no true private. Use @property for getters/setters. class Account: def __init__(self): self.__balance = 0 @property def balance(self): return self.__balance @balance.setter def balance(self, v): if v >= 0: self.__balance = v
Using the abc module: from abc import ABC, abstractmethod class Shape(ABC): @abstractmethod def area(self): pass You can't create objects of Shape; child classes must implement area().

Same method name works for different objects. Duck typing: "If it walks like a duck and quacks like a duck, it's a duck" — Python cares whether an object has the method, not its type. for obj in [Dog(), Cat()]: print(obj.speak())

Special methods with double underscores that give objects built-in behaviour: __init__, __str__ (print-friendly), __repr__ (developer view), __len__, __eq__, __lt__, __add__, __getitem__, __iter__, __call__, __enter__/__exit__ (with-statement).
__str__ – readable output for users (print(obj)). __repr__ – unambiguous output for developers (shown in console/debug). If __str__ is missing, Python uses __repr__.
@dataclass auto-generates __init__, __repr__, __eq__ for data-holding classes (like Java records). from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass class User: name: str age: int
Limits the attributes an object can have and saves memory (no __dict__ per object). Useful when creating millions of objects.
A "class of a class" — it controls how classes are created. type is the default metaclass. Used in frameworks like Django ORM. Rarely needed in daily work.

python.q: How does exception handling work in Python?
python.a: try: x = 10 / 0 except ZeroDivisionError as e: print("Error:", e) else: print("No error") # runs only if no exception finally: print("Always runs") # cleanup
ZeroDivisionError, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError, NameError, FileNotFoundError, ImportError / ModuleNotFoundError, StopIteration, IndentationError.

python.q: How to raise and create custom exceptions?
python.a: class InsufficientFunds(Exception): pass if amount > balance: raise InsufficientFunds("Not enough balance")

python.q: What is a context manager / with statement?
python.a: Automatically sets up and cleans up resources (like closing a file) even if an error happens. with open("data.txt", "r") as f: content = f.read() # file auto-closed after this block Create your own with __enter__ /__exit__ or @contextlib.contextmanager.
r read, w write (overwrite), a append, x create, b binary, + read & write. E.g., rb, w+.

python.q: How to work with JSON and CSV?
python.a: import json, csv data = json.loads('{"a": 1}') # str → dict text = json.dumps(data, indent=2) # dict → str with open("f.csv") as f: for row in csv.DictReader(f): print(row)
Module – one.py file. Package – a folder of modules (traditionally with __init__.py). Library – a collection of packages (e.g., requests, pandas).
Code inside it runs only when the file is executed directly, not when it's imported as a module. __name__ is "__main__" for the running script, and the module name when imported.

python.q: What is pip? What is a virtual environment?
python.a: pip installs packages from PyPI. A virtual environment (python -m venv venv) is an isolated folder with its own Python and packages, so different projects don't clash. Save dependencies with pip freeze > requirements.txt, install with pip install - r requirements.txt.
Marks a folder as a package and can run package setup code. Optional since Python 3.3 (namespace packages), but still commonly used.
os, sys, math, random, datetime, json, re (regex), collections, itertools, functools, logging, pathlib, subprocess, threading, asyncio, unittest.

Counter – count items: Counter("banana") → {'a':3,'n':2,'b':1} defaultdict – dict with default value for missing keys. OrderedDict – ordered dict with extra methods (move_to_end). deque – fast append/pop from both ends (queue/stack). namedtuple – tuple with named fields.

A function that wraps another function to add extra behaviour (logging, timing, authentication) without changing its code. Uses @ syntax. import time, functools def timer(func): @functools.wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
start = time.time() result = func(*args, **kwargs) print(f"{func.__name__} took {time.time() - start:.2f}s") return result return wrapper @timer def work(): time.sleep(1) work() # work took 1.00s Examples in real frameworks: @app.route (Flask), @login_required (Django), @property, @staticmethod.

An inner function that remembers variables from its outer function even after the outer function has finished. def multiplier(n): def mul(x): return x * n return mul double = multiplier(2); double(5) # 10
In Python, functions are objects — you can store them in variables, pass them as arguments, and return them from other functions. That's what makes decorators possible.

python.q: What is the GIL (Global Interpreter Lock)?
python.a: The GIL is a lock in CPython that lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time, even on multi-core CPUs. I/O-bound tasks (API calls, file, DB) → threads still help, because the GIL is released while waiting. CPU-bound tasks (heavy math) → use multiprocessing (separate processes, each with its own GIL). Python 3.13 introduced an experimental free-threaded (no-GIL) build.

Threading Multiprocessing Asyncio Many threads, one process, share memory Many processes, separate memory Single thread, event loop Limited by GIL True parallelism Cooperative multitasking with async/await Good for I/O-bound Good for CPU-bound Best for many I/O tasks (thousands of network calls)

A way to write non-blocking code. async def creates a coroutine; await pauses it while waiting (e.g., for a network response) so other tasks can run. import asyncio async def fetch(n): await asyncio.sleep(1); return n async def main(): results = await asyncio.gather(fetch(1), fetch(2), fetch(3)) # all run together ~1s print(results) asyncio.run(main())

python.q: How is memory managed in Python?
python.a:
1. All objects live in a private heap managed by Python.
2. Reference counting – each object counts how many references point to it; when it hits 0, it's freed immediately.
3. Garbage collector (gc module) – finds and cleans circular references (A → B → A) using generational collection (3 generations).
4. pymalloc – optimized allocator for small objects.
import copy a = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] b = copy.copy(a) # shallow: new outer list, same inner lists c = copy.deepcopy(a) # deep: everything copied a[0][0] = 99 print(b[0][0], c[0][0]) # 99 1
Changing a class or module at runtime (e.g., replacing a method). Used in testing/mocking.
Built-in decorators. lru_cache caches function results — great for recursion like Fibonacci: @lru_cache(maxsize=None).
Tools for efficient looping: count, cycle, chain, combinations, permutations, product, groupby, islice.
Assigns and returns a value in one expression (Python 3.8): if (n:= len(data)) > 10: print(n).
Structural pattern matching, like a powerful switch. match status: case 200: print("OK") case 404: print("Not found") case _: print("Other")
Converting a Python object into bytes (pickle.dumps) and back (pickle.loads) — Python's serialization. Never unpickle untrusted data (security risk).
__getattr__ is called when an attribute isn't found. Descriptors are objects with __get__ /__set__ that control attribute access — @property is built on them.

python.q: What is the difference between append() and extend()?

python.a: list.sort() sorts in place and returns None. sorted(iterable) returns a new sorted list and works on any iterable.
del lst[i] deletes by index; remove(x) deletes first matching value; pop(i) deletes by index and returns it.
import logging logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO) logging.info("Server started") Levels: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL. Prefer logging over print in real apps.

python.q: How do you test in Python?
python.a: unittest (built-in) or pytest (popular, simple assert). Mock with unittest.mock. def add(a, b): return a + b def test_add(): assert add(2, 3) == 5 # run: pytest

python.q: Flask vs Django vs FastAPI? (startups ask) Flask Django FastAPI Micro-framework, lightweight Full-stack, "batteries included
python.a: (ORM, admin, auth) Modern, async, very fast Flexible, choose your tools Best for big apps quickly Auto Swagger docs, type-hint validation (Pydantic)
NumPy – fast arrays and math operations (vectorized). Pandas – DataFrames for table-like data: read CSV/Excel, filter, group, clean. Both are core to data science and ML.

python.a: primes = [n for n in range(2, 50) if all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1))]
